cards.title: Selectivity and Specificity Criteria
cards.claim: Selectivity is the ability to differentiate the analyte from interfering substances in blank matrix. For chromatography, interference response must be no more than 20% of analyte response at LLOQ and no more than 5% of IS response. For LBA specificity, target-analyte accuracy at the LLOQ and ULOQ in the presence of related molecules at their anticipated maximal concentrations must be within ±25% of nominal. Specificity involves differentiating the analyte from structurally similar substances (metabolites, isomers).
conditions: Selectivity evaluated using blank samples from at least 6 sources (chromatography) or 10 sources (LBA).
Haemolysed and lipaemic matrices must be tested if relevant to the study population.
required_inputs: Blank matrix samples from multiple donors/lots.
Interfering substances (metabolites, concomitant meds) at anticipated concentrations.
limitations: Does not guarantee specificity for all possible interferents, only those tested.
Back-conversion of metabolites to parent must be evaluated if relevant.
cards.downstream_use: Ensures measured concentrations reflect the target analyte. Critical for interpreting PK data in complex matrices or when metabolites are active.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
